overview: White plays 1.b4 and Black develops the knight to c6, challenging b4 immediately. White can push 2.b5 or play 2.Bb2 and aim for long-diagonal pressure. I am unsure of the mainline; tags follow the Polish Opening parent, which is sound but rare.

white_ideas.idea: Gain queenside space with b5 or a3

black_ideas.idea: Build a classical centre with ...d5 and ...e5

typical_structures.structure: Flank structure with an advanced b-pawn; flexible centre

character.notes: Flank play with no early forced tactics, so it is steady and unbalanced only in structure.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black comfortable play.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided and the play is on the flanks.

approach.notes: Strong players use the Polish only as a surprise weapon.

level.notes: Unusual structures need understanding, so Intermediate.
